title: Warren Protocol
description: Single source of truth for the Warren wire protocol. Bindings: Headless/internal/output, Headless/internal/api, Headless/internal/server, RelayService/internal/controlplane, Packages/Transport, Packages/Protocol, Web/src/wire.js. The canonical client/server control version is 4.0; binary DENB envelopes remain at wire version 1. This is a coordinated clean break: pre-4.0 clients and persisted protocol state are rejected or reset at the release boundary. Treat this document as authoritative — drift between this file and the bindings is a bug to file against whichever binding diverged first.

logicalVersion.description: Header version reported in the welcome message and used to gate capability negotiation. The v4 client surface is a clean break: pre-4.0 clients are rejected at auth time.

binaryEnvelope.description: Binary DENB frame used for terminal I/O. Stays on wire version 1 while the logical control protocol moves forward. One DENB frame carries one PTY output chunk, one client input chunk, or one opaque atomic terminal-state snapshot.

magic.description: ASCII 'D','E','N','B'. Same magic in Go, Swift, and TS.

wireVersion.description: Independent of the logical protocol version. Bumping this is a hard break — new clients must reject frames from old hosts and vice versa.

atomicState.description: Opaque terminal-state snapshot (e.g. ghostline-vt-replay-v1). Kept as a separate kind so clients can never feed snapshot bytes through their VT output parser.

browserFrame.description: One screencast frame for a Warren Browser Session (RFC 0022). Carries an encoded still image keyed by session and sequence, host-to-client only. It is a separate kind for the same reason atomicState is one: these bytes must never reach a VT output parser, and a browser Session has no PTY at all.

layout.description: Frame layout, big-endian throughout. headerLength covers only the JSON header; payloadLength covers the binary payload. Length fields are u32 BE.

headers.description: JSON header structure for each kind. Decoders must validate that header.payloadLength equals the trailing payload length and reject any mismatch.

jsonControl.description: JSON control envelopes carried as WebSocket text frames alongside the binary DENB stream. Every envelope has a 't' (type) discriminator; the shape of the remaining fields depends on the type.

envelope.description: Client-to-server envelope. Requests carry a method and id; a negotiated app-heartbeat-v1 probe carries t=ping and id without a method.

token.description: Optional pre-upgrade auth token; not the bearer for the WebSocket itself.

terminalStateFormats.description: Opaque terminal-state formats the client can install atomically. The Host picks one and stores it on the peer; mismatched formats terminate the connection.

response.description: Server-to-client response. Discriminated by t; ok=true carries result, ok=false carries error.

session.description: Present on an input rejection (code input_rejected): the terminal the refused DENB input frame was aimed at. DENB frames carry no request id, so this is how the client attributes the refusal.

attachmentId.description: Present on an input rejection (code input_rejected): the attachment identity from the refused frame, or the one the Host expects when it differs.

capabilities.description: Capability identifiers negotiated at welcome time. Order matters — the host returns the intersection in the order the client sent them.

terminalStateFormats.description: Opaque terminal-state encodings the client can install atomically. The Host selects one and reports it back via the attached event.

rpcMethods.description: Catalog of JSON-RPC methods handled on the main WebSocket connection. Each entry lists the canonical name, the params it accepts, and a result reference. Result shapes are described by api/types.go structs in Go bindings.

paramsRef.description: Pointer to the Go struct field shape (or 'free' if the params map is unconstrained).

serverEvents.description: Server-pushed event types. Events do not include a request id. Some carry terminal-session state (attached/synced/recoveryFailed/exited); Agent semantics use the canonical agent.events envelope. The roster event wraps the complete state under state; no migration-era fields are emitted.

welcome.notes: First event after upgrade. Carries the stable Host identity, the authenticated visibility scope, and negotiated capabilities.

maintenance.notes: Sent when the host enters or leaves a maintenance window. Clients should pause long-running work.

auth.notes: Response to the auth envelope; usually sent as the response type, not as a push.

error.notes: Generic error envelope. id is empty when the error is not tied to a request.

roster.notes: Full roster snapshot. Sent on welcome and on full re-sync.

roster.delta.notes: Requires capability 'roster-delta'. Each present collection contains upsert/remove/order arrays; absent collections mean no change. Clients must apply the delta only when baseRevision matches their latest full or delta roster revision. Migration metadata is intentionally absent after the v4 clean break.

attached.notes: Host acknowledges session.subscribe and publishes the attachment identity used by DENB input frames. With capability 'terminal-size-v1', cols/rows give the PTY grid size at (epoch, sequence) when the Host knows it; absent means unknown and no resized events follow for this attachment.

synced.notes: Replay catch-up is complete; the next binary frame will be the live stream at (epoch, sequence).

recoveryFailed.notes: The session.subscribe acknowledgement was already sent, but the Host could not produce the recovery payload (atomic state and paired cursor) for it. The client must cancel any staged recovery for the session and subscribe again; no attached/synced markers follow this event. A failure before the acknowledgement is reported on the command response and never as this event.

resized.notes: Requires capability 'terminal-size-v1' and a sized attached event. Output from (epoch, sequence) on is produced for cols x rows. The event travels ahead of queued output, so clients apply it when their output position reaches sequence, never on arrival.

focusTaken.notes: Another peer claimed this Session's input control lease. The recipient no longer owns it: input it sends is refused by the Host, and it must stop treating its lease as confirmed. attachmentId names the new owner's attachment.

focusGranted.notes: The Host handed this Session's input control lease back to the recipient because the peer that had taken it disconnected and the recipient still wanted it. attachmentId is the recipient's own attachment.

exited.notes: Session has exited and the binary stream for it is closed.

agent.events.notes: The only semantic Agent push. Every event carries eventId, streamId, executionId, sequence, type, timestamps, origin, and typed payload.

pong.notes: Reply to a client ping when capability 'app-heartbeat-v1' is negotiated.

agentEvents.description: Canonical append-only Agent event contract. This metadata is consumed by bindings and contract tests; payload schemas are selected by type.

causedBy.description: The commandId of the client command that caused this event. Host-derived provenance, not part of the event identity: a re-parsed transcript may omit it, and a client must treat it as late-bound rather than as a change to the row. Present on a user message.created when capability 'agent-causation-v1' is negotiated, and on a turn boundary cancelled by an explicit command.

payloads.description: Payload fields per canonical Agent event type. Every field is optional: a payload is an open map, so a provider may add keys this contract does not name, and a client must ignore what it does not read. Declared fields exist so a field's meaning and JSON type have one home; the drift test pins the Host's emitted types against them for the event families listed here.

relayStream.description: BRLY/2 frame format used by the Relay control plane. Distinct wire from the main Host protocol; clients do not decode these directly.

streamClasses.description: Stream class discriminator on the OPEN metadata. 'control' is the duplex host↔relay control channel; 'http' carries proxied HTTP/1.1; 'upgrade' carries the relayed WebSocket upgrade (which is where the inner Host WS lives); 'p2p-signal' is the canonical authenticated signaling class. Relay handshakes advertise and authorize this canonical capability; no unversioned signal alias is accepted.

httpRoutes.description: HTTP routes exposed by the Host. WebSocket upgrades live under /v1/ws; the public Relay-facing endpoints cover health, settings, public access, and Relay join/pairing.
